gen-dafont-reckoner-fs-recia: Recia is a classic serif with a faint modulation you only notice up close, and its openings stay generous. Recia sits under Reckoner's dense, thread-thick sans headings, whose strokes hold steady from stem to curve.
gen-dafont-reckoner-lora: Tight, thick-threaded headlines from Reckoner, then a softer turn. Lora is a classic serif whose joins thin gently at the curves without going spindly, so a long stretch of text moves along with a bookish, unhurried pace.
gen-dafont-rounded-elegance-archivo: Archivo reads like an editorial voice with a friendly face, its curves opening outward instead of curling in. Archivo carries a long passage smoothly, while Rounded Elegance keeps its monoweight headings snug and inviting above it.
gen-dafont-rounded-elegance-fs-literata: Sophisticated and bookish, Literata is a text serif whose thick and thin strokes differ only slightly, with curves left wide open. And Rounded Elegance, with no thick-and-thin contrast to slow the eye, gives the pair its smooth, inviting flow.
gen-dafont-rounded-elegance-fs-paquito: Paquito is a classic serif with a confident, approachable manner and very little gap between its lowercase and caps. Rounded Elegance is best at warm, tightly set headings of uniform stroke, while Paquito holds the text steady beneath them.
gen-dafont-rounded-elegance-fs-supreme: Soft, crowded headings with a monoline stroke meet a body that looks crisp and sturdy, its letters held open rather than curled shut. Supreme and Rounded Elegance share a uniform line, so the sans-serif pair moves together.
gen-dafont-rounded-elegance-fs-trench-sl: Dignified is the first word for Trench Slab, a classic serif whose lowercase sits close to the height of its caps. Trench Slab meets Rounded Elegance, whose uppercase is built from lines of constant thickness, in a refined, warm partnership.
gen-dafont-rounded-elegance-manrope: Manrope is a sans-serif with bright gaps at the mouth of every curve and a line that holds one width throughout. Rounded Elegance shares that build, so its tightly set, warm headings and the text beneath read as one family.
gen-dafont-rounded-elegance-montserrat: Montserrat is a geometric sans with generous white space leading into each curve. Rounded Elegance does warm, tightly packed headings best, while Montserrat does the gliding, wire-like text line, and the two share a similar build.
gen-dafont-rounded-elegance-satoshi: Rounded Elegance sets its warm, monoline letters so close they almost overlap, and Satoshi follows with a soaring x-height. And Satoshi's wide-open e never looks squeezed, so a longer passage moves with the same approachable ease.
